Open Data Apps and Visualizations

The following apps were developed by private third parties or City staff using datasets published on this Open Data Portal. The City would like to showcase work created by others who have given their time to support the community through the creation of applications, while recognizing the tangible results that have resulted from the Open Data Program. Please contact us at opendata@greatersudbury.ca if you would like us to share your work here!



  • CityTransit (App)


    CityTransit (App)

    This transit mobile app was created by Anil Vasani, using the City's Transit open data (myBus API).


  • MonTransit (App)


    MonTransit (App)

    This transit mobile app was created by Mathieu Méa, using the City's Transit open data (GTFS bus schedules and myBus API).


  • Road and Traffic Restrictions (App)


    Road and Traffic Restrictions (App)

    The Road and Traffic Restrictions (RATR) web app was built by the City of Greater Sudbury, using the City's Road Construction open data.


  • Recreation / Récréation (App)


    Recreation / Récréation (App)

    This web app of recreational facilities was built by the City of Greater Sudbury, using the City's Recreation open data.


  • Sudbury Recreational Sites (Map)


    Recreational Sites (Map)

    This map of recreational facilities was built by Dan Scott, using the City's Recreation open data.


  • Sudbury Bus (App)


    Sudbury Bus (App)

    This transit mobile app was created by Logan Pytyl, using the City's Transit open data (myBus API).


  • Sudbury Transit (App)


    Sudbury Transit (App)

    This transit mobile app was created by Steeve St Fleur, using the City's Transit open data (myBus API).


  • WerzmyBus (App)


    WerzmyBus (App)

    This transit mobile app was created by Khairajani Solutions Inc, using the City's Transit open data (CSV bus stops and myBus API).

Anyone can use open data from the City of Greater Sudbury's Open Data Portal at no cost. Download raw data and share your insights with our community or build new applications that serve specific users.

https://www.arcgis.com/sharing/rest/cont.title: Address and Building Roofline
https://www.arcgis.com/sharing/rest/cont.description:
A map and list of addresses in Greater Sudbury. The address point file is a point representation of over 60,000 primary and secondary addresses within the City of Greater Sudbury. Data includes addresses on primary structures (e.g. houses and businesses) and secondary address points which represent buildings that are more than 250 ft. from a primary structure. Updated daily as changes are made to our source data.
  • OBJECTID/ADDRESSID - Simply Unique Identifiers
  • STYPE - Primary or Secondary. Primary identify a place or residence. which represent buildings that are more than 250 ft. from a primary structure. 
  • ADDRESSLIFECYCLESTATUS - Typically Active or Retired. Retired Addresses may occur on lot splits or during address validation exercises
  • ADDRESSALIAS - Where the full text address may have another 'known' name (ex: 3720 Municipal Road 80, 3720 Highway 69 North)
  • ADDRESSNUMBERPREFIX - Prefix to a full text address. ( AddressNumber AddressNumberPrefix Streetname Addressnumbersuffix)
  • ADDRESSNUMBER- The address number,
  • ADDRESSNUMBERSUFFIX - Suffix to the full text address ( AddressNumber AddressNumberPrefix Streetname Addressnumbersuffix)
  • COMMUNITY - Community that the point belongs too.
  • LASTUPDATE - Any time the data point is moved or attribute information is updated this field gets timestamped.
  • CREATEDATE - When the data point gets created this field gets timestamped.
  • ASSIGNEDADDRESSID - The “AssignedAddressID” represents a relationship between addresses and commercial or residential units that fall within. The “AssignedAddressID”, where relevant, will equal the “AddressID” of the appropriate address. 
  • UNIT_OR_AMENITY - Field to aid in filtering data based on the point.
  • UNIT_AMENITY_TYPE - Field to aid in filtering data based on the point.
  • NAME - IF an amenity was collected will contain the name of this amenity (Ex. Schoolnames, restuarant names)
  • VERIFIED_DATE - Simply a timestamp identifying if the City has been requested to verify an existing address.

https://www.arcgis.com/sharing/rest/cont.title: Zoning App
https://www.arcgis.com/sharing/rest/cont.description:
The City is divided into zones, where different land uses are permitted.  These zones are set out in the zoning by-law.  There are zones for residential, commercial, industrial, institutional, rural and other uses. 

Each zone sets out the specific uses that are permitted within the zone and the standards for:

  • minimum lot areas and frontages,
  • setbacks from lot lines,
  • maximum building heights and
  • lot coverage.

 There are also general provisions in the Zoning By-law that can apply across most or all zones such as landscaped area requirements and the amount of parking required for a use.


Le Grand Sudbury est divisé en zones, dans lesquelles différentes utilisations des terres sont permises. Ces zones sont précisées dans le Règlement municipal de zonage. Il existe des zones pour des utilisations résidentielles, industrielles, commerciales, rurales et autres.

Chaque zone établit les utilisations particulières qui y sont permises, ainsi que les normes concernant :

  • la superficie et la façade minimales des lots;
  • la marge de recul des lignes de démarcation;
  • la hauteur maximale des immeubles;
  • la superficie des lots.

 Le Règlement municipal de zonage comprend aussi des dispositions générales qui s’appliquent à toutes les zones ou presque, y compris les exigences en matière d’aménagement paysager et le nombre de places de stationnement requises pour une utilisation particulière.
